correctness.rationale: Removing a minimal element gives a smaller poset; its strict successors form an upper ideal, and adjoining a minimal point below every member of an upper ideal produces a poset. I used this dual enumeration instead of the supplied maximal-element program, deduplicating by the least full relation encoding over permutations within invariant in/out-degree blocks. Counts through eight were 1,2,5,16,63,318,2045,16999; 48346 candidate extensions entered the last deduplication. Joint exact refinement gave 1,2,5,16,63,318,2045,16997 classes and the only nontrivial class sizes were 2,2. For the poset signature, strict lower, strict upper, equality and incomparability exhaust pair types. Incomparability counts are recovered by subtracting the two strict counts and the diagonal from the colour histogram. If histograms differ at any round, the difference persists; when equal, these recovered counts therefore yield the same comparison as full pair-type refinement. Stable colours characterize the C² theories, and size is expressible by counting, so all possible finite competitors are included. I verified that the two frozen witness pairs are strict posets and that their canonical classes match exactly both collisions. Height-two connectivity and the height-three middle multiplicity matrices also distinguish the members without a computer.

evidence: The later November 8 record includes nonisomorphic C²-equivalent posets at every order n≥8 as well as the same first layer. The same-day Boolean-poset result studies B_n and gives a 16-point counterexample for B_4. The earlier literature concerns general identification, not the restricted finite-poset census.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A classification relative to arbitrary binary structures is not a classification relative to transitive partial orders. The Boolean-lattice comparison is narrower and uses a different size parameter. The November 8 theorem does subsume the frozen claim, but its date does not establish earlier priority.

value.rationale: It fixes the first loss of expressive separation for a canonical logic on a standard relational class, and identifies all minimal counterexamples rather than a selected pair. In particular the two witness mechanisms distinguish regular incidence from different middle-incidence multiplicities despite full in/out counting. The exact census and explicit witnesses are usable benchmarks for algorithms and structural classification at the minimal size.
